paths.description: Homepage and results template: primary lottery-results task, global navigation, metadata, network, performance, preferences, accessibility and memory.
Statistics/article index archetype: content listing and mobile navigation.
Alternate results/detail archetype with dense Keno and jackpot tables.
Long-form policy/content archetype used to assess legibility, trust disclosure and narrow-screen reflow.
Failure/recovery journey for an unknown URL.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical in palette and file size to the light capture; computed body background remains rgb(255,255,255), html color-scheme is normal, and no dark scheme is declared.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() tokens for surfaces, text, borders and browser chrome.

findings.summary: Full-page route changes have no authored transition continuity.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero view-transition rules, while the site exposes hundreds of same-origin route links across long result and statistics templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigation, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-state-aware orientation aid.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 11,148 CSS px tall on mobile, but CSS inspection found no scroll-state query/timeline behavior and the visible header does not provide progress or sticky orientation feedback.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep compact primary navigation available on long pages and add a lightweight scroll-state/progress affordance without obscuring content.

findings.summary: Many mobile links have undersized touch targets.
findings.evidence: The 360px focus/target probe measured many meaningful links at only 14–22px high, including province and date links; the recommended target is substantially larger. Keyboard outlines were visible, so the failure is specifically touch sizing.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 24×24 CSS px, preferably 44×44 for primary navigation, using padding and spacing rather than tiny text-only boxes.

findings.summary: Third-party delivery and caching waste delay readiness despite good paint metrics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports TTI 9.6s and 214KiB potential cache savings; the HAR identifies parser-inserted player/DMCA scripts and a 1.6s GTM request.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical third-party scripts, confirm async/defer placement, remove unnecessary dependency chains, and set effective cache lifetimes for stable assets.

findings.summary: The page ships a large amount of unused and legacy JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 499KiB unused JavaScript, 29KiB legacy JavaScript and 14KiB unminified JavaScript; HAR records 731KiB of script transfer out of 804KiB total.
findings.suggestedFix: Load advertising, video, analytics and notification modules only when needed; remove duplicate tags and modernize/minify the remaining first-party bundle.

findings.summary: Data tables and one lookup input lack complete accessible semantics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identifies the Keno table’s fake caption and data cells without headers. The form probe also shows #inputNumberDo has no associated label, relying on placeholder/title.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real <caption>, th/scope headers for result tables, and an explicit visible label associated with #inputNumberDo.

findings.summary: Small targets reduce usability under touch and zoomed/reflowed conditions.
findings.evidence: At 360px, the target probe records dozens of interactive links only 14–22px high, even though the page otherwise reflows without horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target dimensions and spacing while preserving the successful narrow-screen reflow and user-scalable viewport.

findings.summary: The page logs an avoidable Firebase messaging error.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a console.error from notification.services.js: notification permission was blocked (messaging/permission-blocked).
findings.suggestedFix: Do not initialise messaging until the user opts in; treat denied/default permission as an expected state without console errors.

findings.summary: Several images omit intrinsic dimensions and below-fold loading hints.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 3 images without width/height and 2 below-fold images without loading=lazy; one loading asset remains GIF.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions, lazy-load non-critical below-fold imagery, and replace the animated GIF with a lighter modern or CSS alternative where appropriate.

findings.summary: Notification permission is requested on page load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s notification-on-start audit points to notification.services.js line 92; the resulting denial also causes the console error.
findings.suggestedFix: Ask for notification permission only after a clear user gesture explaining the benefit, and keep the site fully usable when declined.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but baseline security headers and cookie protections are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive reports missing CSP, HSTS and nosniff. All four analytics cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None; three persist for 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP, HSTS and nosniff; set Secure and an appropriate SameSite mode on cookies, and shorten analytics retention to what is necessary.

findings.summary: The page has a disproportionate tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 15 third-party origins and five known tracker domains. HAR attributes 42 of 45 requests and 772,761 of 804,382 transferred bytes to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit each third party, remove duplicate/unnecessary analytics and ad calls, gate non-essential tracking on informed consent, and batch/minimise events.

findings.summary: Notification permission is requested without in-context intent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse directly reports notification-on-start and the permission denial error. Authentication was not a covered public flow, so this finding is limited to permission timing.
findings.suggestedFix: Move notification permission behind an explicit, contextual opt-in control and explain frequency and revocation before invoking the browser prompt.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are not configured.
findings.evidence: The response has no clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy, in addition to missing CSP/HSTS/nosniff.
findings.suggestedFix: Set CSP frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and a restrictive Permissions-Policy; add X-Frame-Options as a legacy fallback where suitable.

findings.summary: The manifest declares an app-like standalone experience, but no service worker or offline fallback is registered.
findings.evidence: manifest.json has display: standalone, start_url and icons, yet navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations() returned an empty array and the page was not controlled.
findings.suggestedFix: If standalone installability is intentional, register a service worker and provide a clear offline fallback for cached results/policy pages; otherwise remove misleading app-install signals.

findings.summary: A small set of image-delivery inefficiencies remains.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 3 missing intrinsic dimensions, 2 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 2 images without responsive sources and one legacy GIF.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image space, lazy-load below-fold assets, provide responsive sources where raster content varies, and replace legacy animation formats.

findings.summary: Background analytics and advertising work is chatty and mostly unrelated to the core result task.
findings.evidence: The HAR records repeated Glia pixel requests plus Google analytics/ad collection; 42 of 45 requests are third party, while Lighthouse finds 499KiB unused JS.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove low-value beacons, batch analytics, defer background fetches, and initialise heavy ad/player code only near a visible placement or user action.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts dominate the page’s transfer budget.
findings.evidence: Third parties transfer 772,761 bytes of 804,382 total; GTM, AdSense and the Glia player are the largest offenders, while the primary content is server-rendered text/tables.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove duplicate tags, defer media/player code, and load advertising only when it creates visible user value.

taskList.title: Remove unsolicited permission prompts and harden browser security
Cut third-party, unused and background JavaScript
Repair table, input and touch-target accessibility
Finish resilient installability or remove standalone app signals
Add lightweight navigation continuity on long pages
